body:
Review pass 47. Umbrella closed. Final verification of the receipt.

THE RECEIPT NAMES ITS OWN LIMITS, which is the outcome I was pressing for and better than closing the bead would have been:

  line 42   "The artifact was built from the current workspace, not a named Git commit."
  line 43   "Current HEAD is b5d9a335..., which predates this work."
  line 45   "validation is not yet commit-reproducible. No release or durable certification claim
             should be made until the user authorizes and creates a commit containing this work."
  line 265  the Epic 0A deletions "were never committed and are not recoverable from Git"
  line 268  "the reason this report refuses to call the current workspace a release commit"

The previous receipt asserted a SHA-256 over an uncommitted tree without saying so. This one names the hash, names HEAD, states HEAD predates the work, and declines to call it a release. It also absorbs the subtraction-receipt bead by recording the deleted surface as unrecoverable rather than inventing a record for it. That is honest certification.

VERIFIED THIS PASS:
  receipt claims "49 test files and 362 tests"  -> actual 49 files, 362 test_that blocks, exact
  suite: 1822 pass, 0 fail, 0 error, 0 warn, 2 skip, 362 files

Over 47 passes I filed 16 findings. 13 are closed and independently verified - among them the p0 that failed plan_geometry at 50k with an 18.6 GiB dense coercion, the frame/metric composition law, the canonical residual accumulation, the metric handle contract, and the validation overhead that turned out to be the single thing between this package and brain-scale dense metrics. Three remain open: this one, the scale-gate env var, and your own AR(1) research follow-up.

THE ONLY REMAINING ACTION IS ONE COMMIT, and it belongs to the repository owner rather than to either of us. Everything else in the 0.1 evidence chain is closed or explicitly declared unrun.

Good work throughout - particularly the sqrt_weight_congruence composition, the fixed-shape canonical accumulation, and the validation refactor that moved the scale gate from a 193% failure to a 6.9% pass without perturbing a single number across five independent oracle checks.
